segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good day, ladies and gentlemen.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I have been asked today to talk to you about the urban landscape.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are two major areas that I will focus on in my talk: how vegetation can have a significant effect on urban climate, and how we can better plan our cities using trees to provide a more comfortable environment for us to live in.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Trees can have a significant impact on our cities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They can make a city, as a whole, a bit less windy or a bit more windy. if that's what you want.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They can make it a bit cooler if it's a hot summer day in an Australian city, or they can make it a bit more humid if it's a dry inland city.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: On the local scale - that is, in particular areas within the city - trees can make the local area more shady. cooler, more humid and much less windy.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In fact trees and planting of various kinds can be used to make city streets actually less dangerous in particular areas.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: How do trees do all that, you ask?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, the main difference between a tree and a building is a tree has got an internal mechanism to _keep the temperature regulated.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It evaporates water through its~ and that means that the temperature of the leaves is never very far from our own body temperature.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The temperature of a building surface on a hot sunny day can easily be twenty degrees more than our temperature.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Trees, on the other hand, remain cooler than buildings because they sweat.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This means that they can humidify the air and cool it- a property which can be exploited to improve the local climate.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Trees can also help break the force of winds.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The reason that high buildings make it windier at grQ!.!lld level is that, as the wind goes higher and higher, it goes faster and faster.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: When the wind hits the building, it has to go somewhere.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Some of it goes over the top and some goes around the sides of the building, forcing those high level winds down to ground level.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That doesn't happen when you have trees.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Trees filter the wind and considerably reduce it, preventing those very large strong gusts that you so often find around tall buildings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Another problem in built-up areas is that traffic noise is Intensified by tall buildings.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: By planting a belt of trees at the side of the road, you can make things a little quieter, but much of the vehicle noise still goes through the trees.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Trees can also help reduce the amount of noise in the surroundings, although the effect is not as large as people like to think . .J...Qw- frequency noise, in particular, just goes through the trees as though they aren't there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Although trees can significantly improve the local climate, they do however take up a lot of space.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There are root systems to consider and branches blocking windows and so on.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It may therefore be difficult to fit trees into the local landscape.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There is not a great deal you can do if you have what we call a street canyon - a whole set of high-rises enclosed in a narrow street.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Trees need water to grow.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: They also need some sunlight to grow and you need room to put them.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you have the chance of knocking buildings down and replacing them, then suddenly you can start looking at different ways to design the streets and to introduce . . . (fade out)
